description:
Create the empty flutter_martech package that the bridge code will later go into.

A Flutter plugin has three parts: the Dart API that app developers call, and the iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) code underneath it that talks to MartechKit and MartechPack. This story builds that structure and nothing else. It compiles, it runs, and it does no marketing work yet. The actual bindings come in MTSDK-65, MTSDK-66, MTSDK-67 and MTSDK-68.

It also creates the example app. Every Flutter plugin ships one by convention, and ours has a second job: it is the app the verification suite (MTSDK-47) will run against later. Building it now, while it is empty and cheap, avoids needing a test app later and having none - the problem MTSDK-10 had to work around on native.

Blocked by MTSDK-6: how the package is structured depends on which binding approach that spike picks.

Acceptance criteria:
- flutter_martech builds on both iOS and Android from a clean checkout
- The example app launches on an iOS simulator and an Android emulator in CI
- Codemagic builds and tests it on every PR, green
- Versioning and changelog work the same way as martech-kit and martech-pack (release-please)
- How app teams install the package (pub, git dependency, or private hosting) is decided and written down
- No Martech API is bound yet
